Assume small-deformation, linear-elastic behavior, pure torsion with no axial force, bending, or stress concentration. The shaft is a solid circular cross-section of uniform diameter d over its full length.
The shaft length is L = 1500 mm.
The applied torque is T = 1,000,000 N·mm, acting in pure torsion about the shaft axis.
The allowable angle of twist over the full length L is φ_allow = 0.75 degrees, which must be converted to radians (φ_allow = 0.75 × π / 180 = π / 240 rad ≈ 0.013090 rad) before use in the governing equation.
The material is 6061-T6 aluminum with shear modulus G = 25,939.8 MPa (equivalently 25,939.8 N/mm²).
The polar moment of inertia for a solid circle is J = π d⁴ / 32.
All calculations must be carried out in the consistent N–mm–MPa unit system with no unit conversions beyond the degree-to-radian step.
State the governing torsion relation φ = T L / (J G) explicitly.
Substitute J = π d⁴ / 32 into the governing relation and algebraically solve for d, yielding d = (32 T L / (π G φ_allow))^(1/4).
Substitute the numerical values T = 1,000,000 N·mm, L = 1500 mm, G = 25,939.8 N/mm², and φ_allow = 0.013090 rad into the solved expression.
Show the intermediate computation of the numerator 32 × T × L and the denominator π × G × φ_allow, then compute d⁴, then take the fourth root.
Report the minimum required solid-shaft diameter d in millimeters to at least one decimal place.
State all assumptions used (linear-elastic, small deformation, pure torsion, no stress concentration, uniform cross-section, constant G along the length) in a brief list before the calculation.
The final answer must be a single concrete number for d in mm, not a symbolic expression.
